title: New Zealand Unveils Six-Month Work Visa for International Graduates
excerpt: The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa, opening for applications on November 16, 2026, gives diploma and certificate holders open work rights — a pathway that previously did not exist.
body:
• New Zealand will launch a Short-Term Graduate Work Visa on November 16, 2026, granting six months of open work rights to international graduates at NZQCF Levels 5–7.
  • Applicants must have completed at least 24 weeks of full-time study, demonstrate NZD $5,000 in funds, and apply within three months of their student visa expiring.
  • The visa fills a gap for the nearly 12,000 Indian students in New Zealand, many of whom pursue diploma-level programmes with no previous post-study work pathway.
  • New Zealand is also extending Post Study Work Visa eligibility to Level 7 Graduate Diploma holders who hold a bachelor's degree.

New Zealand will introduce a new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa on November 16, 2026, offering eligible international graduates six months of open work rights after completing their studies. Immigration New Zealand confirmed the launch date in May 2026, following the initial announcement on March 12, according to ICEF Monitor.

The visa targets graduates who hold qualifications at New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF) Levels 5 through 7 — covering certificates, diplomas, and bachelor's degrees — but who do not qualify for the longer Post Study Work Visa. It is designed as a bridge, giving graduates time to secure employment and transition to an Accredited Employer Work Visa for a longer-term stay.

Who Qualifies and What the Visa Allows

To be eligible, applicants must have completed at least 24 weeks of full-time study at a New Zealand institution in an NZQCF Level 5–7 programme. English language, foundation, and bridging qualifications are excluded. Applicants must show at least NZD $5,000 in available funds, meet health requirements, and submit their application within three months of their student visa expiring.

The visa provides unrestricted work rights — holders can work for any employer in any sector without a prior job offer. However, it comes with firm limitations: it can only be granted once, cannot be extended, and is unavailable to anyone who has previously held a Post Study Work Visa. Business ownership is prohibited, and holders cannot sponsor family members for work or dependent child student visas, though partners may apply for visitor visas independently.

"This visa provides 6 months of open work rights, allowing time to look for work and, where appropriate, transition to an Accredited Employer Work Visa."

— Immigration New Zealand

Why It Matters for Indian Students

India is one of New Zealand's fastest-growing source countries for international students. The Indian cohort enrolled in New Zealand grew 99% in 2023 and 49% in 2024, with approximately 12,000 students currently studying there, according to Collegedunia. A significant portion pursues diploma and certificate programmes at NZQCF Levels 5–7, which until now offered no post-study work pathway whatsoever.

The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa directly addresses that gap. For Indian students who completed a one-year diploma in New Zealand and previously had to leave the country upon finishing, six months of open work rights represents a meaningful new option to gain local experience and build a case for employer sponsorship.

Broader Changes to Post-Study Work Rights

Alongside the new visa, New Zealand is extending eligibility for the existing Post Study Work Visa to include Graduate Diploma holders at NZQCF Level 7, provided they also hold a bachelor's degree earned in New Zealand or overseas. The Post Study Work Visa allows holders to work for up to three years and carries broader family sponsorship rights than the short-term option.

Both changes form part of New Zealand's "International Education Going for Growth" strategy, launched in July 2025. The plan targets growth from 83,400 international students in 2024 to 105,000 by 2027 and 119,000 by 2034, aiming to double the economic impact of international education from NZD $3.6 billion to NZD $7.2 billion over the next decade, according to ICEF Monitor. Education-related travel exports already reached NZD $4.5 billion in the year to September 2025.

How New Zealand Compares

The timing of New Zealand's expansion is notable. Canada has tightened field-of-study requirements for its Post-Graduation Work Permit, and the UK is reducing its Graduate Route visa from two years to 18 months starting January 2027. At the diploma and certificate level, New Zealand now offers a formal post-study work option that neither competitor provides.

For bachelor's degree holders, New Zealand's existing Post Study Work Visa — offering up to three years of open work rights — remains competitive with Canada's PGWP and stronger than the UK's shrinking Graduate Route. The new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa adds a lower tier that fills a specific gap, particularly for the diploma-heavy Indian student cohort.

What to Watch

Applications open on November 16, 2026. Prospective applicants should confirm their qualification level falls within NZQCF Levels 5–7, ensure their programme is not classified as a language, foundation, or bridging course, and begin building savings toward the NZD $5,000 financial requirement. With a six-month window that cannot be extended, immigration advisers recommend starting the job search well before graduation.
nri_angle: The visa creates a new post-study work pathway for the nearly 12,000 Indian students in New Zealand, many pursuing diploma programmes that previously offered no route to remain and work after graduation.
